This page installs a single Corium node on a Proxmox host, from the published
qcow2. Every command and every output below comes from a real run on Proxmox
VE 8.4.

The scripts in [`deploy/proxmox/`](https://github.com/Corium-OS/Corium/tree/main/deploy/proxmox)
run on the Proxmox node itself, not on your laptop. This page does not use the
web interface.

## Before you start

- A Proxmox host that you can reach over SSH as `root`. You run every command
  below on that host.
- A storage that accepts snippets. `local` accepts them by default. To find
  out, run `pvesm status --content snippets`. If the command lists nothing,
  add `snippets` to the content types of a directory storage in
  **Datacenter → Storage**.
- A free VMID. `qm list` shows the VMIDs in use.
- Approximately 6 GB of free RAM and 32 GB of free disk.
- The scripts from [`deploy/proxmox/`](https://github.com/Corium-OS/Corium/tree/main/deploy/proxmox)
  on that host. Step 4 runs `create-vm.sh`, and Proxmox does not ship it.
- `corium-agent` on that host, if you want the validation in step 3. No release
  attaches it, so you build it from a checkout. The validation is optional, and
  nothing else on this page needs the binary.

You get both from the same clone:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Corium-OS/Corium.git /root/Corium
cd /root/Corium
mise run build          # writes bin/corium-agent, for step 3
```

The paths below assume that clone. `mise run build` needs Go on the host. If
you do not want Go on a hypervisor, do not run the build, skip the validation
in step 3, and download only the script:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Corium-OS/Corium/v0.5.0/deploy/proxmox/create-vm.sh
chmod +x create-vm.sh
```

## 1. Fetch the qcow2

Run this on the Proxmox host, so that the file is where you need it:

```bash
cd /var/lib/vz/template
curl -fLO https://corium.b-cdn.net/corium-0.5.0-x86_64.qcow2
```

The [release notes](https://github.com/Corium-OS/Corium/releases/latest) give
the exact URL for each release, and the two other ways to download it. In a
real run, 1.5 GB took 15 seconds.

## 2. Check what you downloaded

```bash
sha256sum /var/lib/vz/template/corium-0.5.0-x86_64.qcow2
```

Compare the result with the hash in the release notes. If they match, you have
the bytes that the project published, not only a file that downloaded without
an error. [Downloads](/docs/install/downloads/#check-what-you-got) explains the chain that
makes this true.

## 3. Describe the node

```yaml
#cloud-config
corium:
  role: single
  cluster:
    name: homelab
users:
  - name: core
    sudo: ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL
    groups: wheel
    shell: /bin/bash
    ssh_authorized_keys:
      - ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@example.com
ssh_pwauth: false
```

Save it as `/root/corium-node.yaml`. The other install pages refer to this
`users:` block.
[`examples/single-node.yaml`](https://github.com/Corium-OS/Corium/blob/main/docs/examples/single-node.yaml) is the same
document as a file that you can copy.

Before you boot anything, validate the document:

```bash
corium-agent validate /root/corium-node.yaml
/root/corium-node.yaml: valid (role single, cluster homelab)
```

## 4. Create the VM

> **Warning.** If you set a static address, set `NAMESERVER` too. In Proxmox,
> `ipconfig0` carries only an address and a gateway. So a node with a static
> address comes up with no resolver. The failure is confusing. The node answers
> ping and SSH works, but Kubernetes stops while it pulls images, with
> `lookup quay.io: Try again`. The script warns you, but only if you let it.

```bash
VMID=900 VM_NAME=corium \
  DISK_IMAGE=/var/lib/vz/template/corium-0.5.0-x86_64.qcow2 \
  CLOUD_CONFIG=/root/corium-node.yaml \
  MEMORY=6144 CORES=2 \
  /root/Corium/deploy/proxmox/create-vm.sh
```

The script imports the disk, resizes it, attaches the cloud-config as a custom
cloud-init snippet, and stops:

```
unused0: successfully imported disk 'local-lvm:vm-900-disk-1'
  Size of logical volume pve/vm-900-disk-1 changed from 10.00 GiB to 32.00 GiB.
update VM 900: -cicustom user=local:snippets/corium-900.yaml
update VM 900: -ipconfig0 ip=dhcp

VM 900 (corium) created. Start it with:
  qm start 900
```

`--cicustom` lets the `corium:` block reach the node. It fully replaces the
user-data that Proxmox generates, and does not merge with it.

The defaults are `STORAGE=local-lvm`, `SNIPPET_STORAGE=local`, `BRIDGE=vmbr0`,
`CORES=4`, `MEMORY=8192`, `DISK_SIZE=32G`, and DHCP.

## 5. Start it and find it

```bash
qm start 900
qm guest cmd 900 network-get-interfaces
```

In a real run, the guest agent answered after approximately 30 seconds.

## 6. Watch it become a cluster

```bash
ssh core@<address>
```

```console
$ corium-agent version
corium-agent 0.5.0 (a2575f3)

$ systemctl is-active corium-bootstrap k0scontroller
active
active

$ sudo k0s kubectl get nodes
NAME               STATUS   ROLES           AGE    VERSION
corium-f725a239    Ready    control-plane   2m1s   v1.36.4+k0s
```

In that run, the node took two minutes from `qm start` to `Ready`.

The configuration did not set a hostname, so the agent derived it from the
machine ID. If you want to choose the name, set `node.name`.

`role: single` passes `--no-taints`, so the node schedules ordinary workloads.
The node has no taints, and a pod runs without tolerations.

## 7. When you are done

```bash
qm stop 900 && qm destroy 900
rm /var/lib/vz/snippets/corium-900.yaml
```

`qm destroy` does not remove the snippet.
